Homepage.info: The Red Star Fencing Club was founded to promote and develop fencing in Serbia and quickly became the leading center for this sport. The club has produced many top athletes who have achieved significant results in national and international competitions, fostering team spirit, perseverance, and dedication to fencing.

Weapons.saber_description: The saber is a cutting and thrusting weapon that targets the entire body above the waist, including the head and arms. Saber fencing is the fastest of the three disciplines, characterized by explosive attacks, dynamic footwork, and right-of-way rules that reward aggressive initiative.
Weapons.epee_description: The epee is a thrusting weapon where the entire body is the valid target area. There are no right-of-way rules -- the first fencer to land a touch scores. Epee fencing rewards patience, precise timing, and tactical defensive play.
Weapons.foil_description: The foil is a thrusting weapon that targets the torso (front and back). Foil fencing uses right-of-way rules, requiring fencers to establish priority through their attack before scoring. It emphasizes technique, blade work, and strategic exchanges.
Weapons.saber_target: Upper body above the waist, including head and arms
Weapons.epee_target: The entire body from head to toe
Weapons.foil_target: The torso (front and back), excluding arms, legs, and head
Weapons.saber_rules: Right-of-way applies. Both cutting and thrusting are allowed. The attacker has priority -- the defender must parry before riposting to score.
Weapons.epee_rules: No right-of-way rules. Only thrusting is allowed. Simultaneous touches result in a point for both fencers. Patience and distance control are key.
Weapons.foil_rules: Right-of-way applies. Only thrusting is allowed. The attacker who initiates first has priority. Blade work and technique determine who scores.

ONama.history_1946_text: The Red Star fencing section officially came to life on November 12, 1946, and the section grew into a full club two years later. Red Star fencers quickly earned spots on the national team and diligently promoted this noble sport.
ONama.history_1960s_text: With the arrival of Vera Jeftimijades from the defunct OMK Yugoslavia, from 1960 onward the women's team dominated foil at national championships for the next decade, while the men's team became the undisputed leader in saber from 1970 forward.
ONama.history_1990_text: The club then recorded both excellent and average results, and in the nineties the red-and-white dominance of men in saber and epee was re-established, as well as that of the red-and-white ladies in foil.
ONama.history_1950_section_text: The fencing section expanded into a full club. Under the leadership of Dušan Bogdanović and Jovan Marinčević, the section prospered, with Konstantin Konstantinovich Eger serving as the first coach.
ONama.history_1950_championship_text: Red Star claimed their first team state championship in foil for men at the Yugoslav championship held in Sarajevo, with a team composition of Stanislav Živković, Branimir Živković, Aleksandar Vasin, and Ante Joja. That year the fencing club finally obtained its own premises.
ONama.history_1952_text: The women's team won their first foil title, with team members Vera Marković, Zora Marković, Miroslava Stanojević, and Gordana Cincar Janković.
ONama.history_1955_text: At the State Championship, Branimir Živković became the first individual champion from Red Star in the senior competition in both saber and foil.
ONama.history_1960_text: Vera Jeftimijades joined the club on May 1, 1960, becoming the sole Red Star representative at the 1960 Olympic Games in Rome.
ONama.history_1965_text: The club gained significant reinforcement in 1965 with the arrival of strong fencers from other clubs: Ester Heklai and Piroshka Tisa from OMK Omladić, Zoran Urošević from OMK Železničar, and Stevan Đokić from the Leskovac fencing club.
ONama.history_1970_text: At the Yugoslav Saber Championship held on December 19-20, 1970, in Belgrade, Red Star won the first men's team state title in saber, announcing a 12-year dominance in this discipline.
ONama.history_1976_text: On February 1, 1976, Nebojša Srećković joined Red Star from OMK Željezničar, becoming one of the club's greatest legends and leaving an exceptional mark on the organization.
ONama.history_1989_text: At the Yugoslav Saber Championship held in Zagreb, the men's team won their 14th team title with a composition of Nebojša Srećković, Vladimir Orović, Gábor Besenyi, Vladimir Brajkov, Barija Ebilji, and Branislav Bukvić.
ONama.history_1989_coaching_text: With Nebojša Srećković's assistance, the married couple Yuri and Marina Kuznetsov from Ukraine joined Red Star as coaches and occasionally competed for the club, bringing a qualitative leap in saber fencing.
ONama.history_1991_text: At the Yugoslav Foil Championship for women held in Belgrade, after 12 years of hiatus, Red Star won the state championship title, their 17th in club history. The team consisted of Vesna Krejović, Marina Kuznetsova, Tatjana Babić, Gordana Ilić, and Gordana Rajak.
ONama.history_1997_text: At the regular assembly of Red Star held in 1997, one legend was replaced by another. Miodrag Nikolić Roče became club president following Vera Jeftimijades. He achieved major accomplishments for Red Star by securing the return of the training hall and recruiting the best fencers from Serbia, establishing a golden age of the club.
ONama.history_1999_text: The arrival of Damir Baraljić represented major reinforcement for domestic fencing. In that year, he transferred from OMK Lokomotiva and would bring many titles to Red Star in both team and individual competitions, and later served as club president.
ONama.history_2001_text: Tamara Šotra Savić and Svetlana Višnjić joined Red Star. While Tamara devoted herself to family after winning several state titles, Svetlana Višnjić would achieve unprecedented results: 12 individual and 22 senior team titles in foil, saber, and épée, becoming one of the club's greatest legends.
ONama.history_2004_text: The club was reinforced that year with Bulgarian fencers who were national representatives: Petrom Toshkovim, Theodorom Dundakovim, and Tanja Dimitrovom.
ONama.history_2005_text: Jovan Rajković became the coach in December 2005. His arrival marked one of the best periods in Red Star's history, with the club becoming absolutely dominant in all three disciplines and winning 4 team titles at senior Serbian championships for several consecutive years.
ONama.history_2008_text: Zoran Timić became general secretary, initiating a period of stable club operations that continues to this day. During this period, the club has achieved incredible results.
ONama.history_2009_text: In May 2009, Svetlana Višnjić made a historic achievement at the Serbian Senior Championship by competing in all three weapon categories and winning all three team titles—a feat no one has accomplished since.
ONama.history_2013_text: Following his dedicated work as a trainer and competitor, Jovan Rajković completed his studies and passed the bar exam. Nemanja Đurđić took over trainer duties, with Vladimir Manja beginning his coaching career alongside him.
ONama.history_2013_memorial_text: The Andrej Gardenin Memorial Tournament was promoted on December 8-9, 2013, in the Red Star stadium hall, honoring one of the club's legends. The tournament features pioneer categories in all weapons for both genders.
ONama.history_2015_text: Stevan Koliesov arrived from Ukraine. Through 11 years of dedication, he became a deserved legend of Red Star. That same month, Maria Kovačević won a bronze medal at the senior Balkan Championship in foil.
ONama.history_2016_text: An electoral assembly of Red Star was held on August 16, 2016. Svetlana (Višnjić) Petronjević was elected as the new president, with Zoran Timić continuing as general secretary.
ONama.history_2021_text: In 2021, Veljko Ćuk, undoubtedly the best Serbian fencer of all time, joined Red Star from OMK Vojvodina. In 2022, he won a gold medal at the Mediterranean Games in Oran, Algeria—the greatest achievement of our competitors in history.
ONama.history_2023_text: In September 2023, Petar Volkonskii, a graduate fencing coach from St. Petersburg University and Russian fencing representative, joined the club. That same year, Alim Kadirov, a graduate fencing coach from Moscow University and Russian representative, also joined Red Star. Together with Ivica Subić and Petar Kostadinović, the club now has professional staff in all three weapons.
ONama.history_2024_fie_text: In 2024, club members took significant roles in FIE and EFC governance. Ana Kovrlja became a member of the FIE Judging Commission, Lazar Mičeta became a member of the FIE Medical Commission, and Teodora Višnjić became a member of the EFC Safeguarding and Welfare Commission.
ONama.history_2024_october_text: On October 13, 2024, at the Champions Cup final in Haidenheim, Germany, after epic battles against Italian teams in the semi-finals and finals, Red Star became European runner-up with the team of Muhamed Hamza, Veljko Ćuk, Aleksandar Čupčenić, and Miloš Hrgović.
ONama.history_2025_november_text: At the Champions Cup final in Haidenheim, Germany, Red Star completely dominated the tournament and superior won the European Champions Cup with the team of Muhamed Hamza, Veljko Ćuk, Aleksandar Čupčenić, and Nikita Itkin. Red Star is European Champion.
ONama.history_2025_december_text: Following the proposal of the Savski Venac Sports Association and Red Star Sports Society, Red Star Fencing Club was proclaimed the best club in Belgrade for 2025.
ONama.history_2026_text: Red Star Fencing Club was proclaimed the best club of Red Star Sports Society for 2025.
ONama.values_description: The values that shape generations of Red Star fencers.
ONama.value_discipline_desc: Fencing requires concentration, control, and dedication. At Red Star, we develop discipline that extends beyond the sport.
ONama.value_spirit_desc: Respect for opponents, fair play, and honor are part of the fencing tradition that we cultivate across all generations.
ONama.value_dedication_desc: Continuous work and effort are the key to every competitor's progress. Our trainings build resilience and mental strength.
ONama.value_champions_desc: For more than eight decades, the club develops elite fencers and continues the rich sports history of Red Star.
ONama.cta_description: For more than eight decades, Red Star has been home to elite fencers and new generations of athletes.
